questions.question: Define definite and indefinite loops. Give one Python example for each.
questions.solution_html:
• Define definite and indefinite loops. Give one Python example for each. [A / CO1]
  • Answer: A definite loop executes a fixed number of times (1 Mark) , e.g., a for loop.
  • for i in range(5):
  • print(i) executes exactly five times - (2 Mark)
  • An indefinite loop executes until a condition becomes false - (1 Mark) ,
  • e.g., a while loop. while x (1 Mark)

questions.question: Write the code to compute sample variance of [2,4,4,4,5,5,7,9].
questions.solution_html:
• Write the code to compute sample variance of [2,4,4,4,5,5,7,9]. [An / CO4 ]
  • Answer: Import the statistics module (1 Mark) and use the variance() function (2 Marks) :
  • import statistics
  • data = [2,4,4,4,5,5,7,9]
  • print(statistics.variance(data))
  • It computes the sample variance (sum of squared deviations divided by n-1) (2 Mark) .

questions.question: Write the code to compute determinant and inverse of a 2x2 matrix.
questions.solution_html:
• Write the code to compute determinant and inverse of a 2 ×2 matrix. [An / CO4 ]
  • Answer: Import numpy for linear algebra (1 Mark) .
  • Use NumPy’s linalg functions (1 Marks) :
  • import numpy as np
  • a = np.array([[1,2],[3,4]])
  • print(np.linalg.det(a))
  • print(np.linalg.inv(a))
  • Useful for solving linear systems and matrix computations (3 Mark) .

questions.question: Write a python code for Grade distribution pie chart. Data: A=25, B=30, C=20, D=15, F=10.
questions.solution_html:
• Write a Python code for a grade distribution pie chart.
  • Data [A=25, B=30, C=20, D=15, E=10] [An / CO3 ]
  • Answer: Use Matplotlib to draw a pie chart (2 Mark) :
  • import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
  • grades = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "F"]
  • values = [25, 30, 20, 15, 10]
  • plt.pie(values, labels=grades, autopct="%1.1f%%")
  • plt.title("Grade Distribution")
  • plt.show()
  • Displays the percentage distribution of grades (8 Marks) .

questions.question: Create a dataset of 5 students with 'Name' and 'Gender'. Convert 'Gender' into one-hot encoded columns. [10x2 = 20] HH:MM:SS. tips tip
questions.solution_html:
• Create a dataset of 5 students with ”Name” and ”Gender”,
  • then convert ”Gender” into one-hot encoded columns. [E/CO4]
  • Answer: Create a DataFrame and apply one-hot encoding (2 Mark) :
  • import pandas as pd
  • data = {"Name": ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"], "Gender": ["M", "F", "M", "F", "M"] }
  • df = pd.DataFrame(data)
  • df = pd.get dummies(df, columns=["Gender"])
  • This converts the ”Gender” column into binary columns such as Gender M and Gender F (8 Marks) .
